# NFL realised P&L: where it went, and what is and is not correctable (2026-11-04)

**Aggregate only.** Ratios, counts, z-scores and intervals; no ticker, order id, game, player or dollar figure. Every number is regenerated by

```
python3 scripts/research/fetch_shadow_obs.py --handicap-root /tmp/hd --out /tmp/shadow_obs        # optional, read-only
python3 scripts/research/nfl_wager_loss_structure.py --handicap-root /tmp/hd \
    --closes-root /tmp/md/data/shadow/v2/closes --schedule-csv /tmp/md/data/kalshi/capture/schedule_cache.csv \
    --shadow-obs-dir /tmp/shadow_obs --out-public docs/research/nfl_wager_loss_structure_2026-11-04.json
```

Machine-readable results: `docs/research/nfl_wager_loss_structure_2026-11-04.json`. Research only: nothing here changes a stake, a card, a
threshold, the staking ladder or the risk policy, and nothing is wired into a workflow (a test asserts it).

## Data, and what it cannot do

* **253 owner orders = 243 independent position episodes, weeks 1-8, 140 game-clusters** (parlays are single-ticket clusters), all settled with
  established P&L. Source: the `handicap-data` ledger after the verified-only fee amendments (#243). `stake = price x contracts + fees`; P&L is net;
  fees are counted once.
* **No model probability, thesis, recommendation id or usage projection is recorded with any owner wager.** So "bad handicapping" cannot be
  separated from "fine handicap, bad price" for the owner's decisions. Anything below that speaks about a model uses the **shadow** model's
  point-in-time observations, joined by ticker and time, and is labelled as the shadow model's.
* **True closes** are the published canonical Kalshi closes (weeks 1-7, week 7 partial, week 8 not yet). **No proxy close is computed here**;
  true-close and proxy CLV stay separate. Coverage is stated wherever CLV appears.
* Results were checked against final scores: **99 of 99** derivable full-game outcomes agree with the ledger's settlements.
* Intervals: 95% **game-clustered bootstrap** (4,000 resamples). "Fair-price null": a contract bought at price p pays with probability p; z is
  cluster-robust, and where fewer than 5 wins (or losses) are expected the z is **withheld** and the exact Poisson-binomial win-count tail is used.
  Cells were looked at **after** the results, so a cell that clears Bonferroni is still a lead, not a finding. Multiple-look families are stated.

## Ranked findings

Impact is in points of ROI on outlay (the -19.3 total). "Expected" is what a fix is worth **before** the result is known, if prices are fair
(fees saved), which is the honest benchmark: a realised recovery far above it is hindsight.

## Notes on the method

* **Selection vs structure.** For each held full-game position the control is the mean outcome minus the *ask* of every ladder rung of the same
  series, side and held-side mid within 5c, in other games (median 187 control rungs). Owner = structure + selection exactly. The control comes from
  close prices while the owner paid fill-time prices (mostly the last hour), and its own sampling error is not propagated, so the structure term
  carries no interval here; the market-wide intervals are in item 3.
* **Key numbers.** The margin distribution is a discretised Normal (residual sd 13.27) times a per-margin multiplier fitted on 1999-2022 and tested
  on 2023-2025. The sportsbook line is nflverse's `spread_line`, a **closing** line of another market: it is a stand-in for the line known at the fill and leaks a
  little. The repository's own engines (`nfl_edge/engines`, `nfl_edge/sim/key_numbers.py`) already model key-number mass; the point of item 4 is that the
  **owner's** spread buys look like the product of a fair value that does not.
* **Rung rule.** Every full-game rung settles YES iff the quantity is at least the ticker's number (exchange floor N - 0.5); 99 of 99 comparisons with the ledger agree.
* **Market-wide ladder** (7,188 rungs, 100 games, CLOSE_OK, two-sided, width at most 10c): buying at the ask with an approximate fee of 0.07 p (1 - p) per contract.
  Order-level rounding is ignored, so cost is understated. Moneyline rungs are complementary pairs (mean outcome minus mid is zero by construction) and are excluded.
* **Rule replay** (nine pre-written rules, `nfl_edge/research/wager_selection_rules.py`): train = weeks 1-4, test = weeks 5-8, linear scaling of cost, P&L and fees.
  The Bonferroni interval uses alpha/9 two-sided. Only `min_price_30c` has a test-window interval that excludes zero at that level, and it is the
  rule whose expected value before the result is 0.15 points.

## Rule replay (points of ROI recovered; expected = value before the result is known)

| rule | train (wk 1-4) | test (wk 5-8) | all weeks | expected, all |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| no parlays | +5.2 (CI -2.6 to +16.5) | +3.8 (CI -0.9 to +9.6) | +4.5 (CI -0.2 to +10.5) | 0.4 |
| 5U per bet | +4.3 | -0.7 | +1.8 (CI -3.6 to +9.3) | 0.4 |
| 5U per game | +3.1 | +0.5 | +1.8 (CI -4.8 to +10.2) | 0.5 |
| one position per game | +4.1 | +2.7 | +3.4 (CI -8.7 to +17.6) | 1.9 |
| 30c price floor | +5.0 | +2.75 (CI +0.85 to +5.7) | +3.9 (CI -0.3 to +9.5) | 0.3 |
| no live entries | +0.1 | +3.8 | +1.9 | 0.3 |
| game markets only (no props, no parlays) | +5.8 | +13.4 (CI +0.7 to +26.9) | +9.6 (CI +0.4 to +18.8) | 1.5 |
| structural policy (no parlays + 5U/bet + 5U/game) | +8.3 | +4.3 (CI -2.2 to +11.0) | +6.3 (CI -2.2 to +16.1) | 0.9 |
| spread key-number guard (key-aware edge >= 2c) | +19.3 (CI +3.1 to +37.1) | +1.0 (CI -6.9 to +9.3) | +10.2 (CI +0.8 to +21.2) | 2.1 |

Two rules (30c floor, game markets only) have a test-window interval that excludes zero at the unadjusted 95% level; at the Bonferroni level only the
30c floor does, and its expected value before the result is 0.15 points. Every realised recovery is several times its expected value, which is what
hindsight on fair-priced positions looks like. The rules are *removals* and *shrinks* only; none adds a bet.

## What this PR implements (research only, draft, not activated)

* `nfl_edge/research/wager_loss_structure.py`: the statistics, the key-number-aware margin model and its hold-out, the point-in-time shadow join, the
  selection-vs-structure split, the ladder calibration, the rule replay.
* `nfl_edge/research/wager_selection_rules.py`: nine pure rules over position facts, including the key-number edge guard. Imported only by the research runner and tests.
* `scripts/research/nfl_wager_loss_structure.py` (+ `fetch_shadow_obs.py`) and `tests/test_wager_loss_structure.py` (24 tests: clustered intervals,
  fees once, the fair-price null and its exact tail, tickers and results, margin model hold-out, every rule, shadow-join point-in-time, selection-vs-structure,
  redaction, and a guard that nothing outside research imports the rules).

The **single correction I can stand behind** is a fair-value one: a spread or team-total value must carry key-number mass, because the market does
(item 4, proven on held-out data). What it is worth in profit is 1-2 points if the key-aware edge is right, and that is not yet shown out of sample.
The largest *certain* cost, friction (item 1), has no validated fix because no fill or depth data exist at the moment of a fill.

## Next steps that would settle the open items

1. Record the model probability, run id and recommendation id with every candidate and bet (the CFB report reaches the same conclusion).
2. Freeze the nine rules and the guard now; judge them on wagers placed after 2026-11-04 (weeks 9+), with the same split-free statistic (recovery vs expected).
3. Shadow-measure resting-order fills before any execution change.
4. Publish the week 7-8 closes so CLV coverage returns to 100%.
